entries.test: Whether, as of December 2025, there was little federal AI-specific law, so that preempting state AI laws would leave AI development and deployment mostly without binding regulation.
entries.note: This is an analytic claim that rests on a factual premise: that federal AI law is sparse. 'Mostly unregulated' is loose, but most readers would read it the same way.

This is his own judgment of which justification is acceptable, framed as 'the only excuse I can see'. The factual premise inside it, that the White House is escalating deregulation, is not the claim being asserted.

entries.test: Whether public US polls on AI regulation from 2023–2025 show large majorities in favour of regulating AI.
entries.note: Only the poll half can be checked. The chip-sales half is hedged with 'I doubt' and cannot be graded.

entries.test: Whether, by about 14 December 2025, an executive order had effectively removed state-level AI protections, leaving US citizens with almost no legal recourse against AI harms.
entries.note: The wording is close to hyperbole. The EO signed on 11 December 2025 directed legal challenges to state laws rather than voiding them straight away.

'By the end of the week' plausibly applies only to the first clause; here the hit is tied to the H200 sales, not to a date. 'Take a hit' has no shared measure: it could mean stock price, market share, or competitive position against Chinese rivals.
